resolutions.researcher_notes: 'Okaz' = عكاز = Akkas gas field in Al-Anbar province, western Iraq; the pipeline connects the field to the (still-under-construction) Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant. GEM Status = 'proposed' is well corroborated: the pipeline is not yet built. Per the July 22 2025 Schlumberger/Midland Oil field-development contract, a PARALLEL contract (with SCOP, the State Company for Oil Projects) is to be signed to build a pipeline network linking wells to central processing units, with gas then directed to the Anbar power plant. The National: 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units' (verified). Iraqi News: names the SCOP pipeline-network contract and the 100 mmscfd/Anbar power-plant destination (verified, contains Akkas+Anbar+SCOP). Xinhua: confirms the newly-signed deal to develop the field with output routed to the Anbar power plant (verified). Field currently produces only ~40 mmscfd; the transmission pipeline is planned/to-be-built = proposed. Caveat on independence: all three outlets report the same July 2025 Ministry-of-Oil announcement, but each carries distinct detail (The National's 'long-awaited'/pipeline-to-CPU line vs Iraqi News's SCOP-network specifics), and none cite GEM. Tier high on the value (proposed/planned pipeline). The original current_ref (iraqieconomists.net PDF, Al-Jibawi) returns HTTP 200 but the url_verifier could not extract the 'Okaz'/'Anbar' tokens from it (appears to be a scanned/non-text-extractable PDF), so it is not staged; the three fresh news sources supersede it.
